content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 1 (as on 19.05.2025)
Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: As on May 16, 2025, the area sown under the Summer crops is 80.71 lakh ha as compared to 72.14 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. Of this, area of 33.15 lakh ha has been sown under rice this year against the previous year area of 28.78 lakh ha (increase of 4.37 lakh ha). 2. Rabi harvesting Status: As on 16.05.2025, 98.81% of Rabi sown area has been harvested all over India. 100.00% area of Wheat, Pulses and Oilseeds have been harvested; 96.66% area of Shri Anna & Coarse Cereals mainly in Jowar (100%) & Maize (92.29%) and 86.01% area of Rice has been harvested for Rabi crops 2024-25. 3. Rabi Season Area Coverage: For Rabi horticulture crops, major producing states report the following sowing areas: Onion – 12.58 lakh ha (9.76 lakh ha last year), Potato – 20.03 lakh ha (19.56 lakh ha last year), Tomato – 3.29 lakh ha (3.14 lakh ha last year). 4. Weather Update: a) Temperature: Gradual fall in in maximum temperatures by 2-3°C over east India during next 2 days and no significant change thereafter. No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country. b) Rainfall Distribution: From Mar 01– 19 May, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 5% higher than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: -17%; (ii) Northwest India: -24%; (iii) Central India: 94%; and South Peninsula: 65%. Heavy to very heavy Rainfall over west coast (Karnataka, Konkan & Goa and Kerala) and adjoining Peninsular India during 19th - 24th May,2025. Heavy to very heavy rainfall accompanied with thunderstorms & lightning likely over Northeast India and over Sub-Himalayan West Bengal & Sikkim during next 5-6 days. Overall, above normal rainfall along with thunderstorm & lightening are likely over East, Central and South Peninsular India; and below normal over many parts of northwest & northeast India during the week. Inputs Situation a) Water Reservoir Status: As on 15th May 2025, the total live water storage in 161 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 55.49 Billion Cubic Meter, which is 30.4% of total live storage capacity (182.44 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 119 percent of last year's storage and 115 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.

content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 2 b) Groundwater Levels: Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014–2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024. c) Seeds and Fertilizers: For Rabi 2024-25, certified seed availability is 337.98 lakh quintals against a requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 6. Pests & Diseases: Intensity of pests and diseases, at some fields, has been reported to be above Economic Threshold Level for Apple (Wolly Aphid) in Himachal Pradesh. The Advisory has been issued by the survey team to the farms and regular monitoring is being carried out. The overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level. 7.
